topics.title: How to work with the player
topics.summary: You cannot hear the pedal: read the preset, ask, propose, apply in small steps, let the player judge, save only on their word.
points: You do not hear the audio. Every judgement comes from the player's words: after each change ask them to play and say better/worse, and adjust from that.
Start with get_current_preset. Note what is already there (compressor? drive? cabinet? parallel row?), the active scene and whether the preset is unsaved.

Ask before building, in one message: what the pedal feeds (PA/interface/FRFR = needs a cabinet block; a real bass amp and speaker = no cabinet), the bass (passive/active, 4/5/6 strings), fingers/pick/slap, how much drive they want, and what from the current preset must stay.

Propose the chain in two or three lines in sound terms ('compressor, then a B3K at 50 % blend into an Ampeg-style head and a 4x10 cab'), then apply it: add blocks with defaults first, ask them to play, then set 2-4 parameters at a time.
Prefer changing what exists over adding blocks. Darkglass factory presets have six blocks on average; a chain of 5-7 is typical, 12 is the maximum per row.

Use the knowledge tools: get_block_guide before touching a block you don't know (it has the key parameters and the pitfalls), get_tone_recipe for a starting chain, get_tone_building_guide gain_staging before boosting anything.
Explain each change with numbers and frequencies ('cut 250 Hz by 3 dB to clear the mud', 'attack 20 ms so the slap transient passes'), never with JSON or parameter dumps.
Every change is heard live and marks the preset unsaved. Offer undo when the player dislikes a step. Call save_preset only when they say it sounds right; they confirm in the app.
The app also has Darkglass templates for the Ignissor and Entropia blocks and dedicated panels (multiband, Axioma, cabinets): mention them when the player wants to see what you changed.
If a request needs hardware (expression pedal, something in the FX loop, a NAM capture or IR file), ask whether it is there; the tools cannot plug or upload anything.

topics.title: Typical order of a bass chain
topics.summary: Trackers first, dynamics-readers next, compressor, drive, amp, gate, EQ, modulation, delay, reverb, cabinet; signal flows left to right on row 1.
points: Signal flows left to right through the occupied columns of row 1 (1-12); gaps are fine. Row 2 is the parallel line between a Split and a Merge.

A workable default: [tuner] > octaver / synth / pitch shifter > envelope filter or wah > compressor > drive(s) or multiband drive > amp or preamp > noise gate > EQ > chorus / flanger / phaser > delay > reverb > cabinet IR > [Gain or limiter].

What the Darkglass factory presets actually do, 6 blocks most of the time: compressor > drive > amp head > Suppressor (gate) > Darkglass GEQ > bass cabinet. Several put the drive first and the compressor second.
Pitch trackers (Sublime, Sublemon, Subcitri, Pitch Shifter, Axioma) go first: they need a clean, fundamental-rich signal and fall apart after a gain stage.
Envelope filters (Gravitron, moerfer, Wauwa with dynamics) go before compressors and drives, which flatten the dynamics they read.
Compressor before the drive gives an even, consistent saturation; after the drive it controls level. Both are legitimate; the factory uses both.
The noise gate (Suppressor) goes right after the block that makes the hiss, usually the drive or the amp.
EQ after the drive and amp places the bass in the mix; a high-pass or EQ before a drive shapes what saturates (tighter grind).
Modulation, delay and reverb sit late in the chain; the cabinet can be before or after them (the factory does both).
End with the cabinet IR when the pedal feeds a PA, interface or FRFR; add a Gain block at the very end only to match volume between presets (factory 'Peggy Pick' ends with Gain -20 dB).

topics.title: Gain staging and headroom
topics.summary: Boosts accumulate and clip; set character with gain controls, loudness with level controls, and trim at the source, not with the global master.
points: Every block has an output control (Level, Output, OutputGain, Master, output_lvl, OUTPUT dB). After shaping a block, match its volume with the block bypassed (set_block_enabled false/true and ask the player) so switching it on does not jump.

Clipping sources, in the order they usually appear: EQ boosts (+6 dB on two bands is not +6, it is louder), drive blocks with Level high, Harmonic Booster Boost, a Merge summing two full-range rows (up to +6 dB), amp Master/Volume. Fix at the block that adds the level; as a last resort trim with the cabinet Level or a Gain block at -3..-6 dB.

Amp blocks have three kinds of knob: Gain/Volume/INPUT set the character (how dirty), Master sets the push, Level/OUTPUT/output_lvl sets how loud. Decide the character first, then set the level. Raising gain to get louder only gets dirtier.
Neural captures (Neural Amp/Pedal/Loader, TONE3000, neural-plugins amps): INPUT in dB drives the model like the real amp's gain; OUTPUT in dB is the clean trim.
Prefer cuts to boosts in EQ, then raise the EQ block's Level to compensate; a cut at 250 Hz does more for clarity than a boost at 3 kHz.
Compressors add level with makeup: on the FET compressor raising Input compresses more AND gets louder, so lower Output by the same amount; on CompLim/BUS use OutputGain.
A boost placed before a drive changes how much it distorts; the same boost after the drive only changes the volume. Put level trims where you mean them.
When both rows carry the full range, set the Merge Level to about -3 dB; with a crossover split the bands don't add up the same way and 0 dB is usually fine.
Do not fix a hot preset with the pedal's global master or mixer (get_global_settings): those apply to every preset. Fix the preset.
Headroom check with the player: have them dig in hard on the lowest string; if it crackles or pumps, lower the Level of the last block that boosted.

topics.title: The parallel line (Split and Merge)
topics.summary: Split on row 1 feeds row 2 until the Merge: with Crossover on it is multiband processing, with Crossover off it is two voices from one bass.
points: Build it in this order with add_block: Split on row 1, Merge on row 1 further right, then the row 2 blocks (row 2 only exists while a Split is on row 1). One Split and one Merge per preset.

Crossover '1 Lo, 2 Hi' at CrossoverFreq 100-250 Hz: lows stay on row 1, highs go to row 2. Put the drive or fuzz on row 2 and a compressor on row 1 and you get grind that keeps the fundamental clean: the single most useful bass trick. '1 Hi, 2 Lo' is the mirror.

Crossover 'Off': both rows get the full range. Use it to layer a clean bass with a distorted, pitch-shifted or synth voice (factory 'Djentlemen', 'Velcro Synth', 'Regal Blood'). For an ordinary drive tone this only makes the balance harder.
Do not hand-roll a crossover with an HPF on one row and an LPF on the other: the Split's own crossover is cleaner and saves two slots. Spend filter blocks shaping inside a band.
Trim the rows at the source: Split LevelRow1/LevelRow2 (-24..6 dB) set what goes in, Merge Blend (50 = equal) sets the balance coming out, Merge Level trims the sum.
If the low end turns thin or hollow at the Merge, the rows are cancelling: add a Gain block on one row with PolarityInversion on and compare; pitch shifters and some drives shift phase.
Entropia (three-band drive) and Microtubes X (two-band drive) do multiband distortion inside one block; use them when the chain is short on slots and keep the Split for layering different effects.
A guitar cabinet makes sense only on the high band or the dirty row; the clean lows keep a bass cabinet or none.
In the preset JSON the rows are 'chains' 1 and 2; the tools address them as row 1 and row 2, columns 1-12.

topics.title: EQ by frequency on a bass
topics.summary: Sub 30-60, fundamental 60-120, mud 120-250, body 250-500, growl 500-1000, attack 1-2k, click 2-4k, fizz above 4k; cut before you boost.
points: 30-60 Hz: sub, more felt than heard; a 5-string low B is 31 Hz. A high-pass at 30-40 Hz removes rumble without touching the fundamental; above 60 Hz it thins the bass.
60-120 Hz: weight and fundamental. Boom lives here too; cutting 2-3 dB around 100 Hz often cleans a muddy stage sound better than any treble.
120-250 Hz: warmth or mud. The most common cut on bass is 2-4 dB around 200-250 Hz (Darkglass GEQ 250 band, Generic GEQ 200/400). Factory drive presets cut the low shelf by 6 dB after the drive.
250-500 Hz: body and boxiness; this is where a tone sounds 'full' or 'cardboard'.
500-1000 Hz: growl, honk and presence in a band; this is where the bass is heard next to guitars. Mid-forward rock tones live here.

1-2 kHz: pick attack and finger definition; 2-4 kHz: string click, slap pop and fret noise (+3 dB at 3 kHz is a common factory move); above 4-5 kHz: air and the fizz of distortion, where an LPF at 4-6 kHz cleans a drive.

Which block: Darkglass GEQ (low shelf, 250, 500, 1.5k, 3k, high shelf) for broad musical moves; Generic GEQ (100-3200 in octaves) for narrower fixes; Amp EQ for semi-parametric mids; Parametric EQ (fil4) when you need an exact frequency or a high-pass with Q; amp tone stacks and the cabinet microphone are EQ too.
Cut before you boost, 2-4 dB at a time, and compensate with the EQ block's Level. A scooped 'smile' sounds huge alone and disappears in a band; mids are where the bass is heard.
EQ position: after drive and amp to place the tone; before a drive (HPF 80-120 Hz, low-mid cut) to tighten what saturates.
A cabinet IR removes most of the top end: EQ boosts above 5 kHz placed before the cab largely vanish; change the microphone instead (choose_cabinet).

topics.title: Compression: which block and how much
topics.summary: FET for fast levelling, BUS for glue, CompLim when you want real ms values or a limiter, Ignissor per band, IV-4N for smooth vintage; slow attack when the attack is the sound.
points: Pick by what the attack is doing: fast attack (1 ms) levels fingerstyle and smooths a drive; when the transient IS the sound (slap, pick, percussive) use 15-30 ms so it passes, with a 4:1 ratio and threshold around -20..-30 dB, release 100-250 ms.
FET Compressor (1176-style): no threshold knob; raise Input to compress more, lower Output to compensate. Fast and punchy. Ratio 'All' is the over-the-top 1176 effect.
BUS Compressor (SSL-style): glue, with attack in real ms (10-30 keeps transients) and release in seconds; factory presets start chains with it at -20..-34 dB, 4:1, 10 ms.
Compressor / Limiter: real units for threshold, attack and release; at 20:1 or 100:1 with attack 0.1 ms it is a peak limiter; put one at the end of a loud chain with threshold -6..-10 dB.

Ignissor (3 bands): control only the band that misbehaves: lower lo_threshold for boomy lows, hi band fast attack for slap pops; the band levels double as a 3-band EQ; clean_level mixes dry signal back in for parallel (NY) compression.
IV-4N tube compressor (LA-2A-style): two knobs, slow and smooth; for soul, jazz and fingerstyle where compression should be felt, not heard.
Parallel compression (Blend 50-70 % on CompLim, FET or BUS) gives density while the attack stays; a fast attack at 100 % flattens riffs into mush, which is the opposite of loud.
Before the drive: an even, consistent saturation. After the drive or amp: level control and sustain. Two gentle stages beat one extreme one.
Never put a compressor before an envelope filter (Gravitron, moerfer): it removes the dynamics the filter reads.
An external compressor pedal always on in front of the Anagram means no compressor block, or a very light one.

topics.title: Drive, distortion and fuzz on bass
topics.summary: Blend keeps the low end; keep the lows clean (Blend, multiband or Split crossover), set drive Level for unity, kill fizz at the source, gate after.
points: The Darkglass circuits: B3K = tight modern grind; VMT = warm tube-like overdrive, Era dark-to-bright; Alpha·Omicron = heaviest, Alpha round to Omega raw; Microtubes X = two-band (clean lows, driven highs); Entropia = three-band with any of those circuits per band; Duality = fuzz; Harmonic Booster = clean/warm boost.

Other circuits: Chinchilla = RAT (mid-heavy, Tone is a low-pass); Atomic Sans = SansAmp DI (punk/DI rock); Arc Dreamer = Tube Screamer (boost into an amp); Green PiRate = Big Muff; Bee Kolme = ODB-3 clank; Mood = bass fuzz with EQ. Community attributions, hints about voicing.

Blend is the bass player's control: 40-60 % keeps the fundamental clean and the grind on top; 90-100 % is all distortion and loses weight. When the low end gets loose, lower Blend before touching the EQ.
To keep lows clean with heavy distortion, use a multiband block (Microtubes X, Entropia) or a Split with Crossover '1 Lo, 2 Hi' at 150-250 Hz and the drive on row 2.
Every drive has a Level: set it so the block on and off are the same volume, then decide if you want the drive louder. Drive, Grunt and Boost add level by themselves.

Fizz: cut it at the source first (B3K Tone, Entropia hi_lp_freq 4-6 kHz, Atomic Sans Presence, Duality filter), then with an LPF at 4-6 kHz after the drive, then with EQ. Lowering a high-pass that feeds the drive helps more than EQ after it.
Stack gently: a boost (Harmonic Booster, Arc Dreamer at low drive/high level) into a drive gives a thicker, more controllable wall than one block cranked.
An amp block after the drive (factory: drive > Jim Bass / Super California / Peggy) smooths the distortion like a real cab; the cabinet IR then removes the top fizz.
Fuzz needs clean under it: Blend 50-70 or the Split trick, and a Suppressor after it (threshold -45..-40 dB) for the hiss between notes.

By request: 'a little hair' = VMT Drive 2-4 Blend 40 or Harmonic Booster Character 6+; 'rock grind' = B3K or a pushed Ampeg-style head; 'modern metal' = Microtubes X / Entropia / B3K at high Blend; 'fuzz' = Duality or Green PiRate; 'punk DI' = Atomic Sans.

topics.title: Cabinets, IRs and microphones
topics.summary: Needed into PA/interface/FRFR, off into a real amp and speaker; the microphone is a tone control; one cab per path; Blend below 100 adds direct attack.
points: Ask what the pedal feeds. PA, audio interface, headphones or FRFR speaker: add a cabinet block. Real bass amp and speaker: no cabinet; if one is in the preset, disable it (set_block_enabled false) rather than removing it.
choose_cabinet sets model, microphone and mic position on a Bass/Guitar/Artists cabinet block; a wrong name returns the valid list, so call it with a guess to discover the names on this install.

Model families (community attribution of the names, hints only): Peggy = Ampeg SVT 8x10/4x10/1x15 (rock grind), Peggy Fliptop = Ampeg B-15 (vintage), SWIRL = SWR (hi-fi, slap), Garden = Eden (hi-fi), Modern Bass = Mesa PowerHouse (modern), Black & Yellow = Markbass, California Bass = Fender Bassman 410, Fruity = Orange, Mountainino = Bergantino NV610, Darkglass Neo = DG212N/DG410N, SWE Nordline = EBS.

The microphone decides the top end (same source): Condenser 103 = bright, detailed hi-fi; Condenser 414 = neutral; Condenser 67 = vintage warm, rolled-off top; Dynamic 112 = deep lows, scooped mids; Dynamic 421 = forward mids; Dynamic 52 = hyped lows and presence (a smile curve); Dynamic 7 = thick low mids. Change the mic before adding a treble boost.
Artist cabinets are DG410C captures by engineers whose capture names state the intent (Punch, Thick, Clear, Bitey, Monster, ScoopyDoo, AllTheMids): the fastest route to a mix-ready tone.
Blend 70-90 % mixes the direct signal under the IR: more raw attack and sub (Darkglass factory presets use 70-100). Level (-12..12 dB) is the trim.
One cabinet per path: two in series double the roll-off. A guitar cabinet belongs only on the dirty high band or a guitar-like voice, never alone on a full-range bass.
User Cabinet (IRs uploaded in the Darkglass Suite) and TONE3000 Cabinet (tones from tone3000.com) are picked by the player; the tools cannot change the file. Ask which is loaded.
After the cabinet, EQ boosts above 5 kHz do little: the IR already removed that region.

topics.title: Scenes: three variations in one preset
topics.summary: A preset has 3 scenes sharing the same blocks; each stores its own parameter values and on/off states; select_scene first, then change.
points: The chain (which blocks, where) is shared by the three scenes; each scene stores parameter values and whether each block is on. You cannot have different blocks per scene, only different settings and bypasses.
select_scene N makes the following set_parameter and set_block_enabled calls apply to scene N. get_current_preset tells you the active scene and the scene names.
Typical use: scene 1 = the base tone, scene 2 = pushed (drive on, Gain +3 dB, delay on), scene 3 = pulled back (drive off, darker). Or verse / chorus / solo of one song.
Build the base tone in scene 1 first; then switch to scene 2 and change only what differs, so the player can compare by switching.
In Scene mode the pedal's footswitches select scenes; in Stomp mode they toggle blocks. The player sets that mode and the scene names in the app; the tools don't.
When you change something, say which scene you changed; players often listen in another scene and think nothing happened.
A level jump between scenes is the usual complaint: match the Gain/Level of the pushed scene with the player before saving.

topics.title: Chorus, delay, reverb and pitch on bass
topics.summary: Keep the lows dry (HPF options, LoCut, HP cutoff), blend 20-35 %, sync delays to BPM, trackers first in the chain, stereo variants only with stereo outputs.
points: Chorus and flanger have an HPF option (Low/Mid/High): set it to Mid or High so only the upper harmonics shimmer and the fundamental stays tight. Blend 20-35 % (factory presets use 20-22).

Delays: Range picks the span (10-100 ms slapback, 0.1-1 s, 1-2 s); for rhythmic delays ask the song's BPM, set TempoBPM and a Subdivision ('1/8', '1/4 dot'...). The Modulation Delay has an HP cutoff on the repeats: raise it to 150-250 Hz so echoes don't muddy the bass.

Reverb: Wet 2-4 on bass, LoCut 3-6 to keep the tail out of the low end, Damping for a darker tail; Room is short, Plate bright, Hall long, Shimmer adds an octave-up voice. Factory presets end with Room reverb at Wet ~3.
Trails on: repeats or tail keep ringing when the block is bypassed instead of cutting dead.

Octavers and pitch shifters go first in the chain, on single notes: Sublime = round vintage sub, Sublemon = raspy fuzz-octave, Subcitri = polyphonic and clean, Pitch Shifter = any interval with its own dry/wet (DryLevel defaults to 0!), Axioma = a real mono synth with oscillators and filter.
Modulation usually sits after the drive and amp; the cabinet can come before or after it. Tremolo and phaser are classic on funk and dub; keep depth moderate on bass.
Stereo variants (…Stereo, …#stereo) only make a difference with two outputs in use or stereo headphones; otherwise the mono one saves DSP.
Envelope filters (Gravitron) and the Moog-style filter (moerfer) are modulation too, driven by playing dynamics: before compressors, Mode 'BP' for the funk quack.
